newsitem.title: USA: Mercury hopeful for financing late Monday.
newsitem.headline: Mercury hopeful for financing late Monday.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co, the struggling sub-prime auto lender, on Monday said it was hopeful that it could arrange some short-term financing by Monday afternoon.

"We're hopeful that it could be arranged some time this afternoon," Joseph Kopec, a spokesman for Lake Forest, Illinois-based Mercury, said in a telephone interview. He was referring to about a $50 million financing package.
Kopec said the week-long negotiations with lenders was near completion. "People are signing on waivers," he said. "If somebody raises another issue, it could be protracted."
Published reports said BankAmerica Corp was prepared to offer a $50 million credit package.
Kopec would not comment on the source of the funding, but said "roughly, that's correct in terms of the amount of money."
A spokeswoman for BankAmerica could not immediately comment on the reports.

Mercury defaulted on several million dollars in short-term debt 10 days ago, after the company announced it would have to slash its earnings over the past four years by about $90 million, due to accounting discrepencies.

The company has since hired a turnaround and bankruptcy specialist as chief executive officer, been served a search warrant by FBI agents seeking financial documents and been the subject of more than half a dozen lawsuits by shareholders accusing the company and some officers of securities law violations.
Mercury shares were up 1/4 at 2-1/8 Monday and were the most actively traded issue on the NYSE.
